## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #173, exact head `81d521fc80834ae5d4916140043765fbc65e0414`.

The complete `91e5a85..81d521f` delta is wording-only. No count computation, authentication, recipient routing or delivery flow changes; the prior pass-with-notes and machine-public count boundary remain intact.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new vulnerability identified | - |

Receipt wording removes the delivery-time promise (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:150-157,4928`). The API distinguishes serial-key drain ordering and observed historical timing from a guarantee (`docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:755`); peer guidance is consistent (`skills/pij/references/routes/peer.md:80`). F121's advice is clarified, with its assertion updated (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs:114`; `crates/daemon/tests/directory_http.rs:2577`).

No added FYI sender identities, message bodies, reader audience or C19/C21 disclosure was identified. The aggregate carried count still includes other senders' FYIs but was already readable by the same local bearer via state/events; that prior finding was not retraced or changed.

GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42437402711` and latest successful Delivers run `42437431689` both identify this SHA and success. The earlier cancelled Delivers run is superseded.

No local builds, tests, probes, sends, FYI retrieval, credential reads or mutations were performed.
